task.title: Inspect durable schedules through deterministic JSON
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/817 by exposing typed schedule inventory through a read-only developer CLI.
acceptance_criteria: Add vela-dev schedule inspect for one exact caller-selected database.
Emit one compact deterministic JSON document containing complete typed lifecycle projections.
Return no partial stdout and do not create storage on open, schema, replay, projection, or serialization failure.
Grant no cutoff choice, lifecycle mutation, claim, materialization, dispatch, or execution authority.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused CLI test failed because schedule was an unrecognized subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added deterministic mixed-status, escaping, empty-inventory, missing-database, and non-creation integration coverage.

attempts.diagnostic: Operators needed Rust code to access the kernel projection and could not inspect durable schedules without a practical interface.
attempts.patch: Added schedule inspect, opened only through ScheduleStore::open_read_only, mapped all lifecycle evidence, serialized before output, and emitted one escaped failure diagnostic.

attempts.summary: Verified the complete CLI authority boundary.
attempts.diagnostic: The initial CodeRabbit status was rate limited and therefore insufficient for merge readiness.
attempts.patch: Kept auto-merge disabled until a substantive four-file walkthrough completed with no actionable comments and confirmed deterministic read-only behavior.

outcome.summary: Operators can inspect every durable schedule as deterministic complete JSON without direct SQL or schedule mutation authority.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-dev --test cli

lessons: Build inspection CLIs over typed domain projections instead of duplicating storage interpretation with direct SQL.
Serialize the complete response before writing stdout so failures cannot leave a plausible partial document.
Deterministic ordering and JSON escaping make persisted operational evidence scriptable and safe to compare.
An observation command should omit mutation options rather than relying only on user restraint.
